deepdive.sec: Air Cargo / Dedicated Freighter Airline & Air-Logistics

bull_bear.body: Growth-first: entire ~INR 400cr equity raise (PREF + QIP) earmarked for the 9-aircraft fleet; dry-lease (not purchase) keeps the model asset-light. CFO turned positive (~INR 36cr). Working-capital/tax housekeeping is the weak spot: current tax INR 36cr with **INR 33cr still outstanding**, drawing non-deductible interest (~16–17% effective) despite ~INR 62cr cash — analyst pushed for advance-tax payment; management conceded it as "a point of improvement" for the current year. No dividend discussed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Induction slippage** — FY26 already missed guidance on aircraft-delivery delays; the 4x-fleet ramp is the entire FY27 thesis.
- **War-spike normalization** — March–May demand/rate surge is a "temporary boost"; management argues (COVID analogy) rates settle above pre-war, not back to old normal, and regional air-cargo growth is structural — but a peace/sea-route reopening could soften yields.
- **ATF volatility** — pass-through works only while the industry absorbs surcharges; a prolonged spike could test demand elasticity (management says air has no cheaper substitute as sea freight is also congested).
- **Concentration** — FY26 delivered on just 2 operating aircraft; single home-base (Chennai); some aircraft (VT-AFJ) deliberately grounded post-C-check awaiting contracted Middle-East flying.
- **Working capital / tax** — receivables ~60–80 days; INR 33cr tax outstanding at high interest.
- **Forex/Ind AS** — 60%+ USD billing (INR-depreciation tailwind) but lease-restatement forex losses now hit P&L.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident-to-promotional ("blockbuster," "much more than double," "the only thing that goes up doesn't come down fully is the prices, and we like that"). Credibility check: missed FY26 top-line guidance (1,000→700→583cr) — owned it, attributing to aircraft-delivery delays. Transparent on Ind AS mechanics and cost structure; candid on advance-tax weakness. Guarded/UPSI on Nauru details, 777 routes, and specific contracts — reasonable but limits verifiability. Provided fine-grained operating KPIs (yield, cost/kg, utilization, CTK) which aids tracking.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Two aircraft did INR 583cr** — the operating leverage of adding 7 more (esp. 777s at ~3x a 737) is the whole equation; even "conservative" math points to a step-change.
- **War is a tailwind, not a headwind, for a freighter** — stranded scheduled-airline/belly cargo + Red Sea/Persian Gulf sea-freight congestion pushed volume and rates to Afcom; management frames it as a *boost on top of* already-structural regional air-cargo growth.
- **Designated-carrier status is a quiet cost moat** — the INR 55,000/KL fuel delta on 1-Apr is real margin protection peers without the cert don't get.
- **777 revenue ceiling flagged as conservative** — ~INR 75cr/month/aircraft assumed at 75% load and 14–15 rotations; management explicitly says it can beat this.
- **Ind AS optics** — headline EBITDA/PAT now carry maintenance-reserve and lease-forex noise; normalize before comparing to pre-FY26 IGAAP prints.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Single segment — international dedicated air-freight (dry-lease + charters). **Q4 unit metrics:** yield **USD 2.72/kg**, cost **USD 1.84/kg**, avg rev/trip USD 29,296, 10.76 tons/trip, 23.42 trips/aircraft/week. **FY26 unit metrics:** yield USD 2.54/kg, cost USD 1.58/kg, avg rev/trip USD 31,243, 12.28 tons/trip, 19 trips/aircraft/week. Yield/kg (INR ~229) runs above the IATA industry benchmark (~INR 222). CTK (cargo-ton-km) grew ~82.5% Q1→Q3; Q4 dipped 5.8% QoQ purely due to short-sector charter mix (more trips, fewer ton-km), still ahead of IATA global CTK growth (11.4%). Chennai int'l cargo +12.5% YoY (2.3x the 5.4% all-India rate) — Afcom the main growth constituent. 60%+ of billing is in **USD**.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Designated Indian carrier certification** — a regulatory/licence barrier that gives a fuel-VAT edge (sourced ATF at INR 1,69,000/KL vs INR 2,24,000/KL market on 1-Apr) so cost stays at international parity; not available to non-designated operators.
- **Chennai home-base leadership** — Afcom cited as the main constituent of Chennai's out-performing international cargo growth (+12.5% vs 5.4% all-India), a regional density/relationship advantage.
- **Fuel 100% pass-through** structurally insulates margin from ATF spikes (surcharge mechanism, industry-standard but reinforced by designated-carrier status).
- **Asset-light dry-lease flexibility** — "fast, flexible solutions" let it pivot to high-value charters during the March disruption without owning metal.

latest_quarter.body: FY26 EBITDA margin 40.52% (3-yr: 24.55%→40.52%); PAT margin 20.74% (17.17%→20.74%). FY26 cost split: fixed 39% / variable 48% / other-corporate 13%; total expense INR 434.6cr. Within fixed: aircraft lease rental 36%, maintenance reserve 38%, crew salary/per-diem 13%, insurance 6%, other employee 7%. Within variable: **fuel 62%**, trip support 24%, ground handling 10%, commission 3%, airport charges 2%. Q4 cost-of-revenue: direct 54.4%, depreciation 12.3%, finance 7.3%, employee 2.4%. **Fuel is a pass-through** (fuel-surcharge line item), so ATF inflation is largely margin-neutral; management even argued it can *raise* freight rates as passenger belly-capacity retreats. Maintenance-reserve (per-hour USD accrual, now P&L-charged under Ind AS) and lease-restatement forex losses are the two new margin-optics items.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4FY26 / FY26 (this):** Rev INR 587.7cr (+144%), EBITDA 40.5%, PAT INR 122cr (+230%), EPS 48.65 — on 2 operating freighters; March war spike. Ind AS adopted (first year). Fleet: 3rd aircraft live; 4th/5th narrow-body imminent; **4 B777 wide-bodies fully financed** (PREF+QIP ~INR 400cr) targeting 9-aircraft fleet by H2-CY27. FY26 guidance missed (1,000→700→583cr) on induction delays.
- _Q1FY27 → check: 4th & 5th aircraft operational? FY27 "double+" tracking? 777 induction on schedule (first by Q4FY27, all four by end-CY26)? war-spike yield normalization; advance-tax cleanup; designated-carrier VAT full-year benefit; Noida/Delhi/Mumbai ramp; MRO & Nauru updates._

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth (FY27):** "minimum **double**" of FY26 (~583cr → ~1,160cr+); management repeatedly said "much more than double" and "on a conservative estimate" as capacity more than doubles. No precise number given.
- **Fleet plan:** 3rd aircraft **operational now**; 4th & 5th (narrow-body B737-800) operational "**before the next quarter**" (i.e., early FY27) — "on the way," pending customs on arrival.
- **Wide-body:** **FOUR Boeing 777s** (management corrected an earlier "two" — it is all four); **financial closure for all four done.** At least **one 777 operational by the last quarter of FY27 (Q4FY27)**; all four inducted by **end of calendar 2026**; **full fleet of 9 (5+4) operational by ~mid/second-half of CY27.**
- **777 unit economics:** ~14–15 rotations/month at 75% cargo load factor → each 777 ≈ **3x the revenue of a 737-800**; at current ~INR 25cr/plane/month that implies **~INR 75cr/month per 777** (management confirmed "very conservative").
- **Fuel:** ATF is a **100% pass-through** via fuel surcharge; designated-carrier VAT benefit ≈ **5–7% of fuel cost** (full-year impact from FY27). ATF spiked INR 85,000→2,24,000/KL on 1-Apr; Afcom sourced at INR 1,69,000/KL via designated-carrier status; tapering May→June, expected to "settle to a reasonable level" next quarter.
- **Utilization:** FY26 weekly avg 19 trips/aircraft; target to push beyond, toward industry best (10–14 hrs/day, FedEx/DHL benchmark; Asia-Pac avg 7.9 hrs).
- **Nauru MOU / MRO:** progressing (details UPSI-restricted); MRO activity to "pick up momentum from next quarter," primary objective is third-party MRO (not just in-house).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Demand-led (no formal backlog). FY26 dry-lease revenue **INR 528.71cr**; 1,923 trips; **24,353 tons** carried; **1,129 pure charters** (~⅓ of them in Q4 alone). Q4 dry-lease revenue **INR 160.49cr** on 602 trips (415 pure charters), 1,490 flight hours. March war disruption drove multiple short-sector charters (Chennai–Colombo, Colombo–Male, Chennai–Male) to move stranded westbound cargo. Network: Chennai base (ASEAN focus) + Sri Lanka, Maldives, Middle East (Dubai), Australia-Pacific (Nauru). New tie-ups: **Noida airport (AISATS)** — Afcom to be first cargo aircraft to land at the new Noida cargo terminal; planned entry into **Delhi + Mumbai** international operations.

outlook.body:
- **Wide-body B777 long-haul** — the core re-rating driver (4 units, ~3x a 737 each).
- **MRO business** — in-house + third-party; India cost-competitiveness angle for third-party aircraft maintenance.

- **New gateways** — Noida (first cargo mover), Delhi, Mumbai international.
- **Designated-carrier VAT benefit** — full-year monetization in FY27.

deepdive.thesis: Afcom delivered a blockbuster FY26 — revenue INR 587.7cr (+144%), EBITDA INR 238cr (40.5% margin), PAT INR 122cr (+230%) — on just **two** operating freighters, turbo-charged by a March West-Asia war spike that stranded belly/scheduled cargo and hardened freight rates. The whole story now hinges on **capacity**: management guides FY27 revenue to "minimum double / much more than double" as the fleet scales from 2–3 to 9 aircraft (5 narrow-body B737 + **4 wide-body B777**, financial closure done, fully funded by ~INR 400cr of PREF+QIP). Execution/induction timing is the swing factor — FY26 already missed its own INR 1,000cr→700cr guide (actual 583cr) on aircraft delays.
